title: Warcraft III: Reforged
description:
A Classic Favorite, Reforged. Warcraft III: Reforged is a reimagining of the real-time strategy game that laid the foundation for Azeroth's most epic stories. It is a remake featuring a thorough visual overhaul, a suite of contemporary social and matchmaking features, and more. Command the Night Elves, Undead, Orcs, and Humans as alliances shift and armies clash in this timeless real-time strategy game.

AZEROTH, BORN ANEW!

Experience an Epic Story
The founding of Orgrimmar. The fall of Lordaeron. The reign of the Burning Legion. The rise of the Lich King. Veterans and newcomers alike will experience these pivotal events in Azeroth's history like never before.

The Battlefield Awaits
Play through the points of view of four distinct factions: the mighty Orcs, the noble Humans, the ancient Night Elves, and the insidious Undead. Gather resources, build your base, and assemble an army. Recruit powerful heroes to lead your forces, and meet your foes in battle. Destroy the enemy base to win the game!

Vast Campaigns
Relive the events of Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos and The Frozen Throne. Enjoy an epic saga retold with over four hours of reshot cutscenes and updated voice-overs that breathe new life into the earliest renditions of Azeroth's key characters, across more than 60 single-player missions that span Kalimdor, Northrend, Lordaeron, and beyond.

Reimagined Visuals
Every character, structure, and environment has been recreated to emphasis the depth, dimension, and personality of this rough-hewn fantasy world. Behold Warcraft III's classic units in glorious 4K, with updated animations that bring them to life like you've never seen.

World Editor & Custom Maps
Return to the game that started it all. Discover a vast universe of player-created games, including tower defense, MOBAs, RPGs, survival games, and moreor build your own with the upgraded World Editor.

Multiplayer Matchmaking
Challenge opponents with modern multiplayer matchmaking, search for custom game lobbies, and connect with friends through the Blizzard Battle.net app. With updated UI and countless quality-of-life improvements, its never been easier to get into Warcraft III.

critic_reviews.quote: Excellence demands excellence and Blizzard could have honored its great heritage in a better way. It remains one of the cornerstones of the strategy market, as well as an exceptional experience for any self-respecting video game lover.

Warcraft III: Reforged isn't the game that was promised, but is still a valuable reconstruction of one of the most influential titles in the history of video games. This release is, sadly, riddled with bugs as well as marred by the terrible decisions of Blizzard, particularly that of the false advertising that persists now even after launch. However, despite this, there's little doubting that Warcraft III: Reforged has a compelling story that, even eighteen years on, remains one of the most engaging in the genre. The gameplay holds strong to this day and with the tweaks and upgrades, this is an undeniable diamond in the rough.

Warcraft 3 is such a powerful experience that simply outshines the many flaws of the Reforged operation. Some people wanted a complete remake, others called for #nochanges, and in the end we got the simplest remaster. But it still remains the remastered version of a masterpiece.

Yes, the original Warcraft 3 is still a great game, but it is also clear that Blizzard has missed the mark with this remaster. The singleplayer campaign and gameplay mechanics have aged astoundingly well and the visual update is mostly successful. Newcomers will most likely have a great time experiencing the story and its four distinct races, which are still a lot of fun to play. But where are the vastly improved cutscenes that Blizzard has promised? This is simply not the game that has been advertised. Multiplayer comes with its own problems, from missing features (like a ladder or custom campaigns) to small, but irritating technical issues. Most of it can be fixed, for sure, but it appears rather baffling to me that this is a game from the same studio that brought us masterpieces like Starcraft 2.
Reforged is an uninspiring remaster, but Warcraft 3 itself is still a great game nearly two decades later.

Had Reforged been an optional and free graphical update, undersold and understated and a gift to fans, I doubt there would be any backlash. Instead, Blizzard suggested a revolutionary re-imagining of one of gaming’s most popular titles and failed spectacularly to deliver it. Warcraft III: Reforged does not diminish the core experience that made the game great, but its relatively modest improvements are coupled with some missing features and technical issues that make it a disappointment.

Warcraft III Reforged is at least equal to itself and it is already something. Yes, its graphics engine fails to display a fluidity worthy of the finesse of its redesign. But the game mechanics, the storyboarding of the campaigns and augmented narration convince the player even more that he is facing one of the big names in the history of video games. If you are not a player who is looking to be sharp to enter esports, you will also have a great time online. Don't give in to blind bashing. Form your own opinion.
A successful update of a great game’s presentation, but which removes a number of features that may leave old fans hurting.

To put it bluntly, if you haven't played the classic yet, Warcraft III: Reforged is definitely worth your time, otherwise, wait for a deep discount. The remaster feels rushed with too many things missing or not up to par with what I had expected in terms of improvements. In this state, the best way to describe Warcraft III: Reforged is “serviceable.” Taken as a whole, just like the original, the remaster offers a great gameplay experience for newcomers, but there's not much here that would justify a purchase if you've already played the classic.

Warcraft III is still one of the best RTS ever made, yet this Reforged edition is just a lazy remaster. That’s because many features are missing and the game is plagued by a significant number of technical issues.
The remaster stays far below its possibilities and makes multiplayer worse than in the original. The single-player campaign is still great.

In the end it’s worth noting that when viewing a remake or remaster what needs to be taken into consideration is the source material, how it looks, feels, and plays. That is, in addition to the work carried out to recreate moments, update visuals, and change any of the presentation. To do otherwise would be silly, a terrible game with a wonderful remaster doesn’t warrant a high score. In the case of Warcraft III, the inverse to that is also true. So, what we end up with is something in-between. A classic reborn, in a package that doesn’t warrant all that much in the way of celebration.

The old Blizzard, in fact, wouldn't have shipped the game so quickly at all. There are more sinister changes lurking below the surface, like the inexcusable choice to ruin the original Warcraft III launcher and bring it into the modern era: a cardinal sin.

The highest praise I can give to Reforged is that it’s still Warcraft III. The stellar single-player campaign and strategic multiplayer action are all well preserved here. The updated graphics are a welcome addition, which replaces the original game’s out-of-date visuals with an expressive new look and feel. Unfortunately, the launch version of the game feels far from finished, with bugs and key missing features preventing the current build from being the definitive edition of Warcraft III. It will likely get there eventually, but it’s odd for a remaster to feel like it’s starting from scratch, not presenting an endpoint.
The question therefore arises: why should a Warcraft 3 player buy Reforged?

The initial plans for Warcraft 3: Reforged would have brought the community an ambitious new game, steeped in the classic gameplay and story of TFT & RoC. However, little by little the team started scaling back, starting with the story. Unfortunately, the finished product ended up being not much of an upgrade over the classic version of the game.
An inexplicably careless remaster, where none of the changes are unequivocally for the better and the experience is brought down further by numerous bugs and missing features.

Blizzard has truly shot itself in the foot with this one, as they have no doubt upset the core fan base of this amazing title. This remake should have risen from the ashes and helped Blizzard recover its reputation. In reality, it's likely purged the veterans from their fanbase and will be relying on the game's much-loved campaigns and multiplayer mode to bring in newcomers.

That the best parts of Warcraft 3: Reforged are ripped straight out of 2002 and the worst are the modern changes, however, does not speak highly of the total package that Blizzard has placed on offer in 2020.

Reforged will never be the celebration of one of gaming’s most beloved IPs that it should have been, which is all rather depressing. As is the fact that despite the fun that I’ve had playing Warcraft 3: Reforged and for how it has reminded me what an incredibly influential and brilliant game it is, there’s no way I could recommend anyone outside of the absolute hardcore Warcraft fanbase to purchase it.
Warcraft III: Reforged is built upon such strong foundations, yet manages to be somewhat unremarkable in 2020, mired by technical hiccups and Blizzard’s clumsy messaging.

The difference from the version shown at the 2018 BlizzCon is indeed evident, so much so that Reforged appears as a lazy update, rather than a real "remake". There is no trace of the innovations that would have given an unprecedented cinematographic look to the campaign; even the new user interface has disappeared and the graphic restyling is not enough to cover up stumbling blocks and shortcomings that can only be partially covered by subsequent updating interventions.
This version of Warcraft III has welcome graphical updates to a great game, but it's not reforged enough to justify its price.

Warcraft III: Reforged teaches the harsh lesson that sacred, legendary titles need to be revisited with only the utmost care. Core elements that made the original an absolute Earth-shaker still remain, but as a remaster meant to enhance the original experience, Reforged is greatly flawed.

Warcraft III: Reforged still delivers the same satisfying core gameplay and laudable campaigns, but Blizzard under-delivered on promises and removed features that made the original game something exceptional.

At it's core, Warcraft 3: Reforged is as good, entertaining and addictive as ever. But that core has already turned into a teenager and feels unnecessarily outdated in many respects. This is a game that shows how difficult it can be to revive an immortal classic without stepping on toes.
More of a remaster than a reforge, this remains a quality RTS title, but is a letdown for long-time fans with its lack of new content and Blizzard’s creativity-stifling ownership of custom maps.
An exceptional RTS let down by a very disappointing remaster.

Reforged is just a new way to play the campaign of one of the best games ever made… but that’s pretty much. Blizzard has a lot of work to do to fix this and deliver the remaster the original deserves.
Warcraft III: Reforged is still one of the best RTS ever made, but it's also one of the worst remakes we have seen.
While Warcraft 3 is still a phenomenal game to play today, Reforged is unfortunately a chaotic storm of failed promises, technical bugs and missed opportunities that makes a great game worse.

Warcraft III was a great RTS, and Warcraft III Reforged still is, but has a lot of issues. All races are balanced and the campaign is epic, but this remastered version has a number of issues that cannot be ignored, such as disconnecting from multiplayer or options that were in the original and gone in Reforged.
WarCraft 3 definitely deserves better. The “revamped re-imagination" is disappointing.

So then we are left with Warcraft III, only with a bit nicer figure models and surroundings, and a small bunch of removed elements. If you have the old game from before, it is difficult to say that this renovation is worth the money. And when everything that's gone in Reforged is additionally removed from the old version of the game, it's hard not to scratch our heads and wonder what we're paying for. What's the point?
Warcraft III Reforged could have been a hit remake, but in the end, it's a major disappointment with missing features, a lack of polish, and a lot of promises that failed to materialize.
What was going to be the dream of many fans of the saga ends up being a total disappointment. Only Campaign Mode is saved.

The promise of a glorious remake that everyone could have received a Resi 2-sized boner has turned out to be a nice nostalgia trip for many, but a source of frustration and misunderstanding for others. And that last time is unfortunately a little more justified than your average nerd craze.
It was a dream for many RTS players to enjoy Warcraft 3 with modern graphics. And it seems, it will stay as a dream.

The heavy criticism towards Warcraft III: Reforged has nothing to do with the quality of the experience therein. This remains the wonderful real-time strategy that thousands of people have loved. The real problems begin when you take the changes of this remaster into consideration. The half-baked, unimpressive new engine and hit-or-miss design choices; the numerous bugs and network issues; and, finally, those mind-numbing, corporate-smelling decisions, like the fact that custom maps now belong to Blizzard, or how Reforged effectively ruins the original for those who don't even own the new game.

Warcrast 3 Reforged is a testament to laziness and greedy corporation mentality. Reforged implements just new animations and character models thus classifying the game as a simple remaster rather than a “reforge”. The new EULA, the mandatory usage of the new client (deleting features that existed for over 15 years) and the hefty 30 euros price tag showcase the gloomy practices behind this project.

This new Warcraft III is still a brilliant strategy game, much prettier than before. But it’s also much more broken, full of irritating bugs and broken promises. What’s more, it murdered its older brother.
If you set your expectations a little lower, then Warcraft 3: Reforged is a game worth of your time and money. Sadly, for many of us out there, we were expecting a little more.

Blizzard has addressed some of the complaints and criticism hurled its way, and has promised to work on many of these issues. Naturally, one must ask why the game was released in such a state, especially considering the negative attention the company has garnered over the past year with the reveal of Diablo Immortal and the Blizzard/China controversy.
This wet fart of a release that Activision-Blizzard gave us feels like they’re stepping on my childhood and then spitting in its eye even as the teacher is pulling it off me.

An amazing RTS that deserved a better remaster. Warcraft III is still great, even moreso with the new graphics, but Reforged is a major disappointment because of the lack of polish, broken promises and missing social and multiplayer features.

There’s nothing in Reforged that keeps me hooked in. I was sad playing it. Sad that it ultimately failed. That there are so many things that could have been done better – boldly and with more polish. [03/2020, p.48]

If you’re already a Warcraft 3 fan, this is shaping up to be the absolute best version available , and it’s a real treat to see each new model and map in action. If you’re a World of Warcraft fan who missed out, this is a great opportunity to see the beginnings of characters like Arthas, Jaina, Sylvanas, and Thrall. If you’re an RTS fan, this is a polished take on an important piece of the genre’s history.  [Review-in-Progress]
I’m not angry. I am a little disappointed. I expected Warcraft 3: Reforged to feel new. Instead, it just looks new. [Impressions]

The more I look at this week's launch of WarCraft III: Reforged, the more I shake my head. I've grown up playing Blizzard games for a majority of my life, and while I can think of Blizzard game launches with technical issues or critical shoulder-shrugs, I can't recall a retail launch for a product that, quite simply, wasn't finished. WC3:R changes that.

The game is a mess, and not only that, some of the ways that Reforged is a mess actually impact the original Warcraft III. So even if you didn’t buy the remaster and just want to play your old game, you’ll still face some of the same problems with the new launcher, connecting to servers and so forth. [Impressions]

Reforged ultimately feels like a dusty museum exhibit more than a faithful remaster or an update into the modern age. It could have been an excellent way to introduce this story and game to a new generation...Instead, it’s a halfhearted release that misses the opportunity to bring Warcraft 3 back to its old audience while hopefully finding a new one. Blizzard is aware of the issues, and the offering of an instant refund, no questions asked, to anyone not happy doesn’t seem like a good sign...Reforged isn’t what was promised, and it isn’t what I wanted. Based on the community’s reaction, I’m not alone in that regard.
It’s buggy and it’s a far cry from what Blizzard teased us with back in 2018.

Reforged, like a lot of remasters today, is good for a run around if all you wanted was to give your nostalgia a long leash – long enough to punch some elves in the face, say. But if Warcraft III was a game you not only once loved, but love still; if it’s a game you’ve been playing for the better part of 20 years… Well. It’s not hard to see how Reforged could end up being a bit of a disappointment.

user_reviews.author: JackBlackStack
user_reviews.quote:
An overpriced, unnecessary and oversized mandatory patch originally pitched to fans as an upgrade, Reforged was a serious candidate for the worst remaster of all time, launching in an outright broken state with several key versions missing and worst of all, the original version of the game overwritten and erased in order to promote the inferior new one.

But after six years and scores of patches, is it better? The answer is: Yes! But only in that it advanced from "abysmal" to "mediocre." Still, considering the state of the game launched in, that is a massive improvement. The original features that were lost have all been added back, though the "core" game is still very buggy, and Reforged is still, in my opinion, the inferior version of the game.

However, my opinion on it greatly softened when Blizzard finally, after six years, re-released the original version in the form of a legacy client on Battle Net. This is far and away the best update the game has gotten since RF's launch, because it means buying Reforged gives you access to the original, better version of the game. That alone gives it infinitely more value than it had before

.For putting out a legacy client (like they did for Diablo 2) and bringing Reforged to a much more stable and playable state, I believe Blizzard have earned themselves some kudos. They did a genuinely good thing, and as a reward I'm giving Reforged what may be the highest score from an authentic review on this whole site: a 5 out of 10.

Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos and its expansion, The Frozen Throne, hold an esteemed place in the pantheon of real-time strategy (RTS) games. With their intricate narratives, groundbreaking gameplay, and rich world-building, they laid the foundation for what would later become the immensely popular World of Warcraft (WoW). Therefore, when Blizzard announced Warcraft III: Reforged, expectations soared. However, the final product left many long-time fans, especially those who pre-ordered, with a bitter taste.

Downgraded Visuals:
Despite being marketed as a "reforged" version, many of the in-game graphics and cutscenes did not reflect the quality one would expect from a modern-day remaster. Some character models seemed off, and the visual fidelity in certain areas felt like a step backward from the original.

Broken Promises:
Pre-release promotional material showcased reimagined cutscenes and a more immersive storytelling experience. But what was delivered was far from that promise, making many feel misled.

Technical Glitches:
Players encountered numerous bugs and performance issues upon release. From crashing to freezing, these technical glitches severely hindered gameplay and were uncharacteristic of a Blizzard product.

Classic Version Affected:
What stung even more for some players was that Reforged also affected those who owned the original game. Due to the merging of the classic and reforged game clients, players of the original Warcraft III found themselves contending with many of the same issues plaguing Reforged, without even choosing to buy the new version.

Features Missing:
Several features from the original, such as custom campaigns and LAN support, were inexplicably absent in Reforged. For a game that was supposed to be an upgrade, the removal of beloved features was hard to digest.

Lack of Proper Communication:
Blizzard's response to the community's grievances felt inadequate, leading to further disillusionment. For a company known for its dedicated fanbase and community interaction, the radio silence and perceived lack of accountability were disappointing.

In conclusion, Warcraft III: Reforged had the potential to breathe fresh life into a classic, introducing it to a new generation while satisfying the nostalgia of long-time fans. Unfortunately, it fell short on many fronts. For those who pre-ordered with high hopes, it's easy to understand why they might feel deceived by the final product. It serves as a stark reminder that even the most revered gaming institutions can falter when they deviate from their commitment to quality and their audience.

The game was one of the most anticipated video game remasters, promising to bring back the beloved classic with improved graphics, updated gameplay, and enhanced features. However, upon its release, it became evident that the game fell far short of the expectations set by both longtime fans and newcomers. From technical issues to questionable design choices, here's a comprehensive review of why Warcraft III: Reforged ****.

Broken Promises and Missing Features:
One of the major issues with Warcraft III: Reforged was the substantial discrepancy between the pre-release promises and the final product. Blizzard initially showcased stunning cinematic trailers and touted a complete overhaul of graphics and cinematics. However, when the game launched, many of these features were missing or poorly executed. Several iconic cutscenes were removed, leaving players feeling cheated and short-changed.

Technical Problems and Performance Issues:
Upon release, Warcraft III: Reforged was plagued with numerous technical problems and performance issues. Players encountered frequent crashes, frame rate drops, and connectivity problems, hindering their ability to enjoy the game. Blizzard's failure to address these issues in a timely manner further frustrated the player base, contributing to a disappointing experience.

Downgraded Graphics and Art Style:
While the remastered graphics in Warcraft III: Reforged were initially expected to be a highlight, they turned out to be a massive letdown. The promised overhaul was scaled back, and the visual improvements were not as impressive as anticipated. The new art style failed to capture the charm and atmosphere of the original, leaving players longing for the classic look they loved.

Uninspired Unit and Building Design:
Unit and building design in Reforged also proved to be uninspired. While the developers claimed to have improved models, many units lacked the detail and character of the original, resulting in a bland and lifeless feeling throughout the game.

Disastrous User Interface:
The user interface (UI) in Warcraft III: Reforged was a major point of contention among players. It was clunky, cluttered, and difficult to navigate, making simple tasks unnecessarily complex. This poor UI design hindered the overall gameplay experience and frustrated even veteran players who were familiar with the original game.

Removal of Classic Version:
One of the most baffling decisions made by Blizzard was the forced upgrade to Reforged, which left players with no option to play the classic version of Warcraft III. Many fans preferred the original experience, and the absence of this option alienated a significant portion of the player base.

Lack of Content and Support:
Warcraft III: Reforged lacked the additional content and support that players had hoped for. The game shipped with minimal new features and failed to introduce any compelling post-release updates or expansions, causing the game to quickly grow stale.

Conclusion:
In conclusion, Warcraft III: Reforged was a massive disappointment that failed to deliver on its promises and left fans feeling betrayed. Technical problems, downgraded graphics, uninspired design, and a lack of essential features all contributed to a lackluster gaming experience. Blizzard's mishandling of the remaster alienated a passionate community and showcased a lack of care and dedication to one of its most cherished franchises. Warcraft III: Reforged is an unfortunate example of how not to handle a classic game remaster.

user_reviews.author: Hochbichler
user_reviews.quote:
Warcraft III: Reforged is an 2020 attempt at remaking the classic legendary RTS Warcraft III. Before saying anything about the game itself, please allow me to clarify how I see and review remakes. I cannot possibly give a remake credit for any aspects of the game that remains completely unchanged from the original. Those aspects were already reviewed and praised (or hated) in the original game. So I only take into consideration aspects of the game that are new or actually were remade. Now about this disastrous game. Everyone remembers the horrible release and rightfully angry fans. Back then I wanted to retain my sanity and I decided to wait with playing this game. But now, almost three years later, I wanted to see how bad or good the game actually is. I really did not want to pay for this game, but luckily it has gotten cracked this summer. Now, first disappointment came right after I started the game. The menu is different and it just is not nearly as cool as the original menu, including the campaign menu little animated scenes. Remember the Reign of Chaos chilling menu music? That is gone for some reason. Then I started the campaign to see the graphics, that was, after all, the whole point of the remake. At first sight, It seemed ok, they got the colors and the textures mostly right. What I did not like were the units and especially the heroes. In my opinion their textures have too excessive details that you cannot appreciate from the RTS view and on the contrary, a lot of units seem pretty similar to each other and sometimes it might be difficult to tell one unit from the other. The heroes have new armor and clothes from the WoW and it mostly just does not look good at all. If I think about the graphics in general, it looks to me more like a 2010 remake then a 2020 one. One more thing about the graphics, all the icons are new, which seems redundant and confusing. New autosave system is also pretty useless. Also the developers wanted to distinguish the dreadlords among themselves, and it did not went great. Poor Anatheron and Detheroc, more like breadlords. No wait, I can do better. Also the developers wanted the game to sell in China and plus sexism is bad, mkay, so not even a hint of nudity or anything suggestive, the harpies animated icons got zoomed in on their heads. But those are all graphical aspects and sadly the developers decided to fick with the gameplay also. In short, everything they touched is more or like destroyed. The game is filled with bugs even now, three years after release. Not game breaking, but certainly noticeable and immersion breaking. Compare that to the bug-less original. Now a little thing about the difficulty. I consider myself a Warcraft III veteran and I have played hundreds of competition games back in the day, so I was truly surprised that some missions really took me by surprise and made me reload and rethink my strategy (I was playing on Hard difficulty). Now that would be fine, I would even welcome it, but the game does it in such a random and idiotic way that I cannot find any joy in it. Plus there is no balancing, some missions are really easy, some are really hard. What an excrementshow. One minor plus is that they resisted and did not included any SJW elements, like, you know, female orcs/taurens or footwomen. Thank god for that at least. No microtransactions, but the whole game should have been free as an homage to the great fans. Instead they charged 30 bucks for it.

All these bugs would not in fact make a terrible game, more like a mediocre one. But what is the most horrible and disgusting thing is the Activision Blizzard's greed, immorality and depravity. The have no shame and it looks like the long fall from grace is not over yet for this once beloved company. I wish they would just stop taking these legendary great games and ruining them, but I know that is not going to happen. Final Verdict: 1 %
